content: The test image shows a field-level view of soybean with scattered yellowing/browning of leaves and uneven canopy — some plants appear normal green while others show premature yellowing. This field pattern suggests a systemic or soil-borne disease. Top candidates: Sudden_death_syndrome, Soybean_Cyst_Nematode, Phytophthora.

Based on my analysis:

**Test image observations:**
- Field-level overview of soybean crop
- Scattered yellowing/browning of leaves throughout the canopy
- Uneven plant height/density — some areas appear lighter/more yellow (especially mid-to-back field)
- No sharp disease patches, more diffuse yellowing

**Reference comparison:**
- **Sudden_death_syndrome**: Field view in reference shows very similar scattered yellowing throughout canopy with some areas more affected; SDS is known to cause this field-level interveinal chlorosis/premature defoliation pattern
- **Soybean_Cyst_Nematode**: Shows similar diffuse yellowing but tends to show more stunted plants in patches along compaction/soil lines
- **Brown_Stem_Rot**: Shows more localized death patches — doesn't match
- **Phytophthora**: More damping-off/wilting pattern — doesn't match

The diffuse field-level yellowing with browning scattered through an otherwise green canopy, particularly the lighter-colored/yellowing middle-to-background zone of the field, closely matches the Sudden Death Syndrome field reference pattern.
